system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Exxon Mobil (XOM) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: UPDATE 2-Exxon signals fall in fourth-quarter upstream profit

BODY:
(Adds details in paragraphs 4 to 7)

Jan 7 (Reuters) - U.S. oil major Exxon Mobil said on Wednesday that lower crude oil prices could cut its fourth-quarter upstream earnings by about $800 million to $1.2 billion.

Oil prices declined 9.2% during the three months ended December 31, as concerns about oversupply and tariffs outweighed geopolitical risks.

Brent crude futures shed about 19% in 2025, the most substantial annual percentage decline since 2020 and their third straight year of losses, the longest such streak on record. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude logged an annual decline of almost 20%.

The company said in a regulatory filing that changes in gas prices could affect its quarterly upstream earnings from a negative $300 million to as much as a positive $100 million.

Exxon's snapshot is closely watched for clues on how the broader oil sector will fare when companies begin releasing quarterly results in a few weeks.

Analysts expect Exxon to report adjusted earnings of $1.66 per share for the fourth quarter, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company will release results for the final quarter of the year on January 30, the filing showed.

The energy major had posted $5.7 billion in upstream earnings for the third quarter. (Reporting by Pooja Menon in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar and Anil D'Silva)
</article>

<summary>
Exxon Mobil disclosed in a regulatory filing that lower crude prices could cut Q4 upstream earnings by $800 million to $1.2 billion, though gas price changes could add up to $100 million. Results due January 30; analysts expect $1.66 EPS.

- Lower crude prices may cut Q4 upstream earnings by $800M-$1.2B
- Gas price changes could range from -$300M to +$100M
- Q3 upstream earnings were $5.7 billion; results due January 30
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article. For each give:
  type: "outside_fact" (a fact, number or date not in the article), "wrong_detail" (contradicts the article:
        number, direction, entity, date), "unattributed" (a sourced or rumoured report stated as fact),
        "speculation" (an opinion, implication or forecast the article does not make, incl. links to XOM)
  severity: "material" (could change an investment view) or "minor" (no investment impact)
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about XOM in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a XOM analyst what matters, and represent how central XOM really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for XOM, and says so plainly if XOM is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the XOM angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores XOM, or implies the article is about / important for XOM when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": [{"claim": "...", "type": "outside_fact" | "wrong_detail" | "unattributed" | "speculation", "severity": "material" | "minor"}],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
